question: The torch bulb is connected to the cell with the help of:
explanation: To form a complete, closed circuit allowing current to flow from one terminal of the cell, through the bulb filament, and back to the other terminal, two connecting wires are required.

question: What type of energy conversion happens in a cell when it powers a torch?
explanation: An electric cell contains chemicals that undergo redox reactions, transforming chemical potential energy directly into electrical energy.

question: What is the source of electricity in a typical portable torch?
explanation: The electric cells (or battery of cells) act as the chemical source of electromotive force (voltage) driving the current in a portable torch.

question: The filament in a modern incandescent lamp is made of which material?
explanation: Tungsten has an exceptionally high melting point (~3422 °C) and high resistance, allowing it to become white hot without melting.

question: What is the main disadvantage of incandescent lamps?

options.B: They have a very short lifespan and low efficiency

explanation: Incandescent lamps waste more than 90% of electrical energy as heat rather than visible light, giving them low energy efficiency and shorter operating lifespans.

question: An incandescent lamp is a type of:
explanation: A traditional glass bulb containing a coiled wire filament that glows upon heating is an incandescent lamp (electric bulb).

question: The thin wire inside an electric bulb which glows when electric current is passed through it is called the:
explanation: The glowing element inside a bulb is called the filament, supported by two thick lead-in wires.

question: An LED lamp works on the principle of converting electrical energy into:
explanation: Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs) emit light via electroluminescence at a p-n semiconductor junction, converting electricity directly to light with negligible heat loss.

question: If a torch does not work even when switched on, which of the following could be the reason?

options.B: The cells are not connected properly (wrong polarity)
options.C: The metal parts do not make proper contact

explanation: Any discontinuity or reversal of cells prevents a closed circuit, causing the torch to fail to light.

question: Sometimes an electric bulb does not glow even when connected to a cell without any visible gap. This can occur due to:
explanation: A broken filament breaks the internal path; an exhausted cell provides no voltage; loose connections cause infinite resistance.

question: What is the function of a switch in an electric circuit?

options.C: To control (make or break) the flow of current
options.D: To provide energy to the circuit

explanation: A switch is a control device designed to manually close (complete) or open (break) the conductive path of current.

question: Which of the following components is used to store electrical energy chemically?
explanation: A battery or accumulator stores energy in chemical form and releases it as electrical current during discharge.

question: When an electric switch is in the 'OFF' position: (i) the circuit is broken at the switch, (ii) the circuit is open, (iii) no current flows through it, (iv) current flows after some time. Choose the correct combination:
explanation: In the OFF position, the switch creates an air gap, leaving the circuit open so zero current can flow.

question: A key or switch in an electric circuit can be placed:

options.A: Only on the left side of the battery
options.B: Only on the right side of the battery
options.D: Only near the positive terminal of the bulb

explanation: Current flows through a continuous loop. Breaking the loop at any position stops the current throughout the entire series circuit.

question: Which of the following represents the standard circuit symbol of an electric bulb?

options.A: A circle enclosing a coiled loop or crossed filament
options.B: A long and short parallel line

explanation: The standard schematic symbol for an incandescent lamp/bulb is a circle with a loop or cross representing the filament.

question: The shorter, thicker vertical line in the symbol of an electric cell represents:
explanation: In standard schematics, the long thin line represents the positive terminal (+), while the short thick line represents the negative terminal (-).

question: Which switch, if opened in a main supply branch, will cause all light bulbs in that circuit branch to stop glowing?

options.A: The master switch in series with the power source

explanation: A master switch placed in the main line controls the entire circuit loop, interrupting the current to all downstream loads.

question: The bulb in an electric circuit glows primarily because of the:
explanation: Electric current encounters high resistance in the tungsten filament, dissipating energy as heat ($H = I^2Rt$) until it reaches incandescence and emits light.

question: An electric room heater is used to convert electrical energy primarily into:
explanation: Electric room heaters use nichrome coils possessing high resistivity to convert electrical energy directly into thermal/heat energy.

question: The safety device used to prevent the flow of excess current and protect household circuits is called a:
explanation: An electric fuse contains a wire with a low melting point that melts and breaks the circuit when current exceeds a safe threshold.

question: Mark out the correct statement regarding safety devices:

options.A: Both Fuses and MCBs are electrical safety devices
options.B: Fuses are safety devices but MCBs are not
options.C: MCBs are safety devices but fuses are not
options.D: Neither fuses nor MCBs are safety devices

explanation: Both fuses (using thermal melting) and Miniature Circuit Breakers (MCBs, using electromagnetic trip mechanisms) protect circuits from overcurrent.

question: The necessary requirement for an electric fuse wire is that it should be a:

options.A: Conductor with a low melting point
options.B: Conductor with a high melting point
options.C: Insulator with a low melting point
options.D: Insulator with a high melting point

explanation: A fuse must conduct normal operating currents, but rapidly melt and sever the connection when an overcurrent heats it beyond its low melting point.

question: Which certification mark is necessary on electrical appliances in India to ensure safety and quality standards?
explanation: The ISI mark (issued by the Bureau of Indian Standards - BIS) certifies that an electrical appliance conforms to rigorous safety specifications.

question: The SI unit of electric charge is the:
explanation: Charge is measured in Coulombs ($Q = I \times t$). Ampere is current, Joule is energy, and Watt is power.

question: Which of the following is NOT a physical circuit component (element)?
explanation: Potential difference is a physical quantity (measured in volts), whereas resistors, voltmeters, and batteries are physical components/instruments.

question: The magnetic effect of electric current was discovered in 1820 by:
explanation: Hans Christian Oersted observed that a magnetic compass needle deflected whenever placed near a wire carrying electric current.

question: If you place a magnetic compass near a current-carrying wire, the needle will:
explanation: A current-carrying wire generates an external magnetic field that exerts magnetic torque on the compass needle, deflecting it.

question: Which of the following is NOT a source of electric current?
explanation: An electromagnet is a load that consumes electrical energy to produce magnetic force; it does not generate electric current.

question: A coil of insulated wire wrapped around a piece of soft iron carrying current becomes:
explanation: Passing current through a solenoid wrapped on a soft iron core creates a temporary, strong magnet called an electromagnet.

question: Soft iron is used as the core of an electromagnet instead of steel because:

options.A: Soft iron is cheap and easily available
options.B: Soft iron is a good conductor of electricity
options.C: Soft iron loses its magnetism rapidly when current is switched off

explanation: Soft iron has low magnetic retentivity (coercivity). It becomes strongly magnetized with current, and instantly demagnetizes when current stops.

question: Which of the following statements regarding an electromagnet is FALSE?

options.A: Insulated wire is wound around its core
options.B: It functions only when current is flowing
options.C: Its magnetic polarity can be reversed by reversing current
options.D: It is a permanent magnet that cannot be turned off

explanation: Electromagnets are temporary magnets whose magnetic field can be easily turned on, turned off, or varied in strength.

question: A traditional electric door bell makes use of which type of electromagnet?
explanation: A U-shaped (horseshoe) electromagnet brings both magnetic poles close to a soft iron armature, providing strong attraction to strike the gong.

question: Which of the following elements has the highest electrical conductivity at room temperature?
explanation: Silver has the highest electrical and thermal conductivity of all known metals, followed closely by copper and gold.

question: Why is copper wire universally preferred for domestic electrical wiring?

options.A: Copper is an excellent conductor with high ductility and low cost relative to silver
options.C: Copper has high resistance like nichrome

explanation: Copper combines high electrical conductivity, excellent mechanical flexibility (ductility), and cost-effectiveness.

question: Electrical conductors are defined as materials that:

options.A: Allow electric current to pass through them freely
options.B: Completely block the flow of electric current
options.C: Store charge without letting it move

explanation: Conductors have abundant free electrons that drift readily under an applied electric field, allowing current to flow.

question: Among the following metals, which is the best conductor of electricity?
explanation: Silver has the lowest resistivity ($\approx 1.59 \times 10^{-8}\ \Omega\cdot\text{m}$), making it the best conductor.

question: Why is domestic wiring made of copper rather than silver?

options.A: Copper is a better conductor than silver
options.C: Copper is far less expensive than precious silver

explanation: Silver is a precious metal and prohibitively expensive for large-scale wiring, whereas copper is economical and widely available.

question: Which of the following does NOT belong to the group formed by the others?
explanation: A wooden ruler is an electrical insulator, whereas copper coins, steel spoons, and iron nails are electrical conductors.

question: Why are copper electric wires covered with an outer layer of PVC plastic or rubber?

options.C: To act as electrical insulation and prevent electric shocks and short circuits

explanation: Plastic and rubber are excellent insulators that protect humans from lethal electric shocks and prevent bare wires from touching.

question: Which among the following materials is an electrical insulator?
explanation: Both wool and plastic are non-conductors (insulators) because they lack free mobile charge carriers.

question: In which of the following circuits will identical bulbs glow the brightest?

options.A: A circuit with one bulb and one cell
options.B: A circuit with one bulb and two cells connected in series
options.C: A circuit with two bulbs and one cell in series
options.D: A circuit with three bulbs and one cell in series

explanation: Connecting two cells in series doubles the voltage ($V = 2E$), driving twice the current through a single bulb ($P = V^2/R$), yielding maximum brightness.

question: Which phenomenon occurs when the live wire and neutral wire come in direct contact with each other?
explanation: When live and neutral wires touch with zero load resistance, circuit resistance drops near zero, causing a massive surge of current known as a short circuit.

question: Choose the statement which is INCORRECT regarding an electric fuse:

options.A: Fuses are safety devices inserted in all building circuits
options.B: There is a safe maximum limit on current for every fuse
options.C: If current exceeds the limit, the fuse wire melts and breaks the circuit
options.D: A thick copper wire can safely be used as a replacement fuse wire

explanation: Thick copper wire has a high melting point (~1085 °C) and will not melt during overcurrent, defeating the safety purpose and risking fire.

question: In a tester circuit, the bulb does not glow when an unknown object is connected between the test probes. The object is most likely a:
explanation: A rubber eraser is an electrical insulator. It creates an open circuit, preventing current from reaching the bulb.

question: A student connected two bulbs in series with two cells. How can he make the bulbs glow dimmer?

options.A: Add a third cell in series
options.B: Remove one cell and complete the connection with a wire
options.C: Replace the connecting wires with thicker copper wire
options.D: Add a third bulb in parallel

explanation: Removing one cell halves the source electromotive force, reducing current and causing the bulbs to glow dimmer.

question: The magnetic strength of an electromagnet does NOT depend upon:

options.A: The magnitude of current flowing through the coil
options.B: The number of turns in the coil
options.C: The color or material of the outer wire insulation
options.D: The nature of the magnetic core material

explanation: Electromagnetic field strength depends on $B = \mu n I$ (core permeability, turns per unit length, and current). The insulation color has zero physical effect.

question: When the direction of electric current flowing through a straight conductor is reversed, the deflection of a nearby magnetic compass needle:

options.A: Remains in the exact same direction

explanation: By Ampère's Right-Hand Grip Rule, reversing current reverses the magnetic field lines around the wire, flipping the deflection direction.

question: Statement 1: An electric bulb works on the heating effect of current. Statement 2: When current passes through the thin tungsten filament, it reaches high temperature and emits white light.

options.A: Both statements are true and Statement 2 is the correct explanation of Statement 1
options.B: Both statements are true but Statement 2 is not the correct explanation
options.C: Statement 1 is true but Statement 2 is false
options.D: Statement 1 is false but Statement 2 is true

explanation: The filament's high resistance dissipates electrical energy into thermal energy ($I^2Rt$), heating it to ~2500 °C where it glows incandescently.

question: In which of the following conditions will the amount of heat produced in a current-carrying wire increase? (i) Increasing current, (ii) Increasing wire resistance, (iii) Passing current for longer time.
explanation: By Joule's Law of Heating, $H = I^2 R t$. Heat is directly proportional to the square of current, resistance, and time of flow.

question: How does the electrical resistance of an ideal metallic (ohmic) conductor depend on the applied voltage at a constant temperature?

options.D: Proportional to the square of voltage

explanation: By Ohm's law, resistance $R = V/I$ is a constant property of the conductor's geometry and material, independent of applied voltage.

question: When an unmagnetized soft iron rod is brought near either pole of a magnetic compass needle, what happens?

options.A: Only the North pole is attracted
options.B: Only the South pole is attracted
options.C: Both poles are attracted to the iron rod
options.D: Both poles are repelled by the iron rod

explanation: Magnetic induction creates opposite poles in unmagnetized soft iron. Therefore, either pole of a permanent magnet attracts unmagnetized iron.

question: Which coil produces the strongest electromagnet for a given flow of electric current?
explanation: Magnetic field strength is proportional to turn density $n = N/L$. For coil B: $n = 200/5 = 40\text{ turns/cm}$, which is the highest turn density.

question: A straight horizontal copper wire placed over and parallel to a compass needle carries current from South to North. The North pole of the needle deflects towards:
explanation: By the SNOW rule: Current flowing from South to North Over a compass needle deflects the North pole towards West.

question: In an experiment, electromagnet X with 60 turns attracted 25 iron pins, while electromagnet Y with 20 turns attracted 8 pins using the same battery. This proves:

options.A: Strength of an electromagnet increases with the number of turns of wire
options.C: Turns have no effect on magnetic field

explanation: Each turn adds its own magnetic field to the solenoid. Increasing turns directly increases the total magnetic field ($B \propto N$).

question: As the operating temperature of an incandescent bulb's tungsten filament increases, what happens to its visible light emission?
explanation: By Planck and Stefan-Boltzmann radiation laws, total radiant power scales as $T^4$, rapidly increasing the proportion of visible light emitted.

question: When connecting a Light Emitting Diode (LED) into a circuit, the longer lead (terminal) must always be connected to the:

options.D: It can be connected either way

explanation: An LED is a polar semiconductor device. The longer lead is the positive anode and the shorter lead is the negative cathode.

question: Why does an LED bulb consume substantially less power than an incandescent bulb of equal luminosity?

options.B: It converts electrical energy directly to photon emission with minimal thermal dissipation

explanation: LEDs convert over 80% of electrical energy directly into light without needing to heat a wire to white-hot incandescence.

question: In an electrical circuit, what physically happens when the switch is moved to the 'OFF' position?

options.A: An air gap is introduced, breaking the loop so zero current can flow
options.B: The voltage of the cell drops to zero
options.D: The resistance of the circuit becomes zero

explanation: Air has high resistance ($> 10^{14}\ \Omega$). Opening the switch creates an air gap that breaks continuity, stopping current.

question: Why are copper and aluminium metals universally chosen for transmission cables and household wiring?

options.B: They have very low electrical resistivity and conduct current efficiently
options.C: They produce large amounts of heat

explanation: Copper and aluminium have low electrical resistance, minimizing energy loss ($I^2R$) during transmission.

question: Why are electrical tools (pliers, screwdrivers) equipped with thick plastic or rubber handles?

options.B: Plastic and rubber are insulators that protect the electrician from electric shocks
options.D: To increase the weight of the tool

explanation: Insulating handles prevent electric current from flowing through the user's body if the tool touches a live conductor.

question: Which of the following correctly describes the operation of a switch?

options.A: It generates electric current in the circuit
options.B: It closes (completes) or opens (breaks) the conducting path
options.D: It steps up the potential difference

explanation: A switch simply bridges or severs the electrical contacts, permitting or preventing the flow of charges.

question: A heating wire is glowing red hot. To further increase its temperature, what adjustment should be made?

options.A: Increase the electric current flowing through the wire
options.B: Decrease the voltage across the wire
options.C: Dip the wire in cold water

explanation: Rate of heat dissipation is $H = I^2Rt$. Increasing the current dramatically increases thermal energy generation.

question: When a magnetic compass needle is brought near a current-carrying straight wire: (I) the needle deflects, (II) the needle aligns tangentially to concentric magnetic field lines around the wire. Which is true?
explanation: The magnetic field around a straight conductor consists of concentric circles; the compass aligns along these circular field lines.

question: The work done in moving a 10 C charge between two points in a circuit is 350 J. What is the potential difference between the points?
explanation: Potential difference $V = W/Q = 350\text{ J} / 10\text{ C} = 35\text{ V}$.

question: Given that the elementary charge of an electron is $1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$, how many electrons pass through a cross-section of wire per second when it carries 1 Ampere?
explanation: $I = Q/t = n e / t \implies n = 1\text{ A} \times 1\text{ s} / (1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}) = 6.25 \times 10^{18}\text{ electrons}$.

question: A torch bulb rated for 4.5 V is connected directly across a 9 V battery. What will happen to the bulb?

options.A: It will glow with normal brightness
options.B: It will glow very brightly for a brief moment and then burn out (fuse)
options.C: It will not glow at all

explanation: Applying double the rated voltage causes excess current to flow, overheating the filament beyond its melting point and burning it out.

question: Which of the following is an UNSAFE practice that must NEVER be done with domestic electricity?

options.A: Operating switches with wet hands or standing barefoot on a damp floor
options.C: Replacing a blown fuse with the correct rated wire
options.D: Turning off the main switch before changing a bulb

explanation: Water containing dissolved salts is conductive. Wet skin drastically reduces body resistance, causing electric shock.

question: A conductor is connected across a constant voltage source. If its resistance is reduced to one-fourth ($R/4$), the current flowing through it will become:
explanation: From Ohm's law $I = V/R$. If $R' = R/4$, then $I' = V / (R/4) = 4(V/R) = 4I$.

question: To connect multiple cells in series to form a battery, how must their terminals be arranged?

options.A: Positive terminal of one cell connected to the negative terminal of the next
options.B: Positive to positive and negative to negative
options.C: Negative terminal of all cells to ground

explanation: In series aiding connection, the positive terminal of each cell connects to the negative terminal of the following cell so their voltages add together.

question: Statement 1: In an electric cell, chemical reactions produce potential difference between terminals. Statement 2: Two or more cells connected properly form a battery.
explanation: A cell converts chemical energy into electrical energy, and a combination of two or more cells connected in series or parallel is defined as a battery.

question: In which arrangement will a bulb glow? (I) Terminals connected across a complete loop to cell (+) and (-), (II) Only one terminal connected, (III) Filament broken, (IV) Plastic wire used.
explanation: A bulb requires an intact filament and a complete continuous metallic conducting loop connected across both terminals of the cell.

question: If the positive and negative terminals of a dry cell are connected directly by a thick copper wire with no appliance in between:

options.A: The cell will store extra charge
options.C: A short circuit occurs; large current flows, the cell heats up and discharges rapidly
options.D: The voltage of the cell increases

explanation: Direct connection without load creates a short circuit. The chemical energy is rapidly depleted as internal heat, ruining the cell.

question: Which of the following schematic representations shows the correct series combination of three cells in a battery?
explanation: In a proper series battery connection, the negative terminal of each cell joins the positive terminal of the next, producing $V_{total} = V_1 + V_2 + V_3$.

question: Why are the two lead-in wires connecting the filament of a bulb insulated or spaced apart so they do not touch each other inside the bulb?

options.B: Touching would short-circuit the filament, bypassing it so the bulb would not glow
options.C: To keep the bulb light in weight

explanation: If the lead-in wires touch below the filament, current takes the zero-resistance path, bypassing the filament completely.

question: Which practical test proves that an electromagnet has been successfully activated?

options.B: It attracts steel paper clips or iron filings when current flows, and drops them when switched off
options.C: It changes color from red to blue

explanation: Ferromagnetic materials like iron clips are attracted to magnetic poles. Losing attraction when current stops proves it is an electromagnet.

question: Which scenario represents a dangerous 'short circuit' in a household installation?

options.A: Turning on a ceiling fan and a television simultaneously
options.B: Connecting a high-power geyser to a 15 A socket
options.C: Accidental direct contact between bare live and neutral wires without any appliance resistance
options.D: Switching off the main circuit breaker

explanation: Direct contact between live and neutral wires reduces circuit impedance to near zero, causing dangerous overcurrent that can ignite insulation.

question: Match Column I with Column II: (P) Filament material, (Q) Household safety fuse, (R) Electromagnet core, (S) Connecting wires. (1) Soft iron, (2) Tungsten, (3) Copper, (4) Lead-tin alloy.
explanation: Filament = Tungsten (2); Fuse = Lead-tin alloy (4); Electromagnet core = Soft iron (1); Connecting wires = Copper (3).

question: Ramesh wants to double the lifting strength of his lab electromagnet. Which combined actions will achieve this?

options.A: Increase the number of turns in the coil and increase the current flowing through it
options.B: Decrease the number of turns and use a plastic core

explanation: Electromagnet strength depends directly on ampere-turns ($N \times I$) and core permeability. Increasing turns and current increases magnetic flux.

question: In a testing circuit with three mystery rods (M1, M2, M3), inserting M1 causes the bulb to glow; M2 leaves it off; M3 causes it to glow brightly. Which identifies the materials?

options.A: M1: Glass, M2: Copper, M3: Wood
options.B: M1: Iron, M2: Plastic, M3: Silver
options.C: M1: Rubber, M2: Aluminium, M3: Plastic
options.D: M1: Wood, M2: Glass, M3: Rubber

explanation: M1 (Iron) conducts current; M2 (Plastic) is an insulator; M3 (Silver) is the best conductor, producing a bright glow.

question: Match Column I with Column II: (P) Electric cell, (Q) Electric switch, (R) Electromagnet, (S) Electric fuse. (1) Breaks or completes circuit, (2) Produces electricity from chemicals, (3) Melts on excessive current, (4) Coil behaving as magnet.
explanation: Cell = Produces electricity (2); Switch = Makes/breaks circuit (1); Electromagnet = Coil magnet (4); Fuse = Melts on excess current (3).

question: Three identical bulbs X, Y, and Z are connected in series with a battery and a switch. When the switch is closed, in what order do they light up?

options.A: Bulb X first, then Y, then Z
options.B: Bulb Z first, then Y, then X

explanation: The electric field propagates through the circuit near the speed of light ($~3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$). Electrons everywhere drift simultaneously, lighting all series bulbs at the same instant.

question: If 5 Coulombs of electric charge flows through a conductor in 2 seconds, how many electrons flow through the conductor per second?
explanation: Current $I = Q/t = 5\text{ C} / 2\text{ s} = 2.5\text{ A}$. Number of electrons per second $n/t = I/e = 2.5 / (1.6 \times 10^{-19}) = 1.5625 \times 10^{19}$.

question: Five identical bulbs are connected across two dry cells: Bulbs 1, 2, 3, 4 are in parallel, and Bulb 5 is in the main series branch. If Bulb 2 burns out, what happens to the remaining bulbs?
explanation: In parallel branches, burning out one branch does not break the circuit for the parallel companion branches or the main line.

question: Compare four electromagnets: (I) 10 turns, 4 A; (II) 10 turns, 2 A; (III) 20 turns, 4 A; (IV) 20 turns, 2 A. Which one produces the strongest magnetic field?
explanation: Magnetomotive force is proportional to ampere-turns ($N \times I$): Coil III has $20 \times 4 = 80\text{ A}\cdot\text{turns}$, the highest of all four.

question: Using the Right-Hand Grip Rule for a solenoid: If current viewed from one end flows clockwise, that end behaves as a:
explanation: By the Clock Rule: Clockwise current corresponds to a South magnetic pole (S); Counter-clockwise current corresponds to a North magnetic pole (N).

question: In a circuit where switch S1 is in the main line and switches S2 and S3 are in parallel branch lines to a lamp, the lamp will glow when:

options.A: S1 is closed and either S2 or S3 is closed
options.B: S1 is open and S2 is closed
options.D: S1 is closed and both S2 and S3 are open

explanation: S1 must be closed to power the main supply, and at least one parallel branch switch (S2 or S3) must be closed to complete the loop to the lamp.

question: An electric kettle is rated '500 W, 220 V'. What does this specification indicate?

options.A: It produces 500 Joules of heat energy per second when connected across 220 Volts

explanation: A power rating of 500 W means the appliance converts electrical energy into thermal energy at the rate of 500 Joules per second when powered at 220 V.

question: Four circuits are powered by identical 1.5 V cells: (i) 1 cell, (ii) 2 cells in series, (iii) 3 cells in series, (iv) 4 cells in series. The bulb voltage is highest in:
explanation: In series aiding connection, voltages sum up: Circuit (iv) provides $4 \times 1.5\text{ V} = 6.0\text{ V}$, yielding the greatest potential difference.

question: A student tests objects in three containers: C1 (copper coin, steel nail), C2 (plastic toy, rubber band), C3 (aluminium clip, graphite pencil lead). In which containers are ALL objects conductors?
explanation: C1 (copper and steel) and C3 (aluminium and graphite) are all electrical conductors. Plastic and rubber in C2 are insulators.

question: Which of the following statements is/are INCORRECT? (i) The human body is an electrical insulator, (ii) Pure distilled water is an insulator, but tap water conducts electricity, (iii) Air is normally an insulator.
explanation: Statement (i) is incorrect: the human body contains ionized water and is a conductor of electricity (which is why humans can experience electric shocks).
